subject: Call summary + model-fit & JSON schema next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ellie James <ellie.james@helixthera.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@helixthera.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Oct 2029 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Discovery + proposed eval plan

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the open discussion on the Helix integration goals. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Summary (what we heard)
- Goal: move from human-routed triage to an LLM-driven triage + structured extraction for clinical intake forms (reduce manual work, preserve auditability).
- Key constraints: strict structured output (JSON schema), ability to detect & surface schema violations, and tolerance for occasional fuzzy text for free-text fields.
- Compliance items: SOC 2 evidence, insurance cert, and NDA for deeper perf artifacts.

Initial model fit suggestions (recommended starting point)
- Redwood-llama-13b-quant-v2 (cost-optimized; good extraction accuracy at 512 tokens)
- Mistral-Instruct-22B (higher accuracy for complicated extractions; fallback for low-confidence cases)
- open-llama-7b-qa (cheap lightweight fallback for short fields)

Benchmarks & artifacts we’ll share
- Quick snapshot: helix_bench_snapshot.csv (attached) — token breakdown and sample latency profile
- Prompt sets & structured-output testcases: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bHelixEval
- JSON schema test vectors: jsonschema_testcases.jsonl (attached)

Structured-output / function-calling notes
- We’ll treat this as structured-output first (JSON responses that must validate against your schema). If you want function-calling later we can add the tool interface.
- Error handling plan: for schema failures, the runtime will return a structured error envelope (error_code, invalid_path list, original_response) so your service can decide to retry or surface to human.
- Retry guidance: idempotency keys + exponential backoff (max 3 tries) for transient errors. We’ll include recommended header patterns.

Proposed eval plan & timeline
1) Sandbox access & NDA: we’ll get the DocuSign NDA sent today (request from Tom).
2) Smoke run (48h): run JSON schema compliance suite against 1k samples to measure raw schema pass-rate and types of failures.
3) 14-day evaluation: two model variants (redwood-13b-quant primary, mistral-instruct fallback) across representative prompt sets. We’ll collect p50/p95 latency, schema pass-rate, and quality regressions vs. your gold labels.

Immediate asks from Helix
- Can you confirm the procurement contact and expected timeline for SOC 2 / insurance?
- Do you want us to enforce strict schema rejection (fail fast) or return best-effort JSON + error envelope?

Next steps (for our side)
- I’ll loop in Monica to provision a sandbox with test credentials and a smoke-run harness.
- We’ll attach the initial bench snapshot and the JSON test vectors (see attachments).

Attachments: helix_bench_snapshot.csv (csv), jsonschema_testcases.jsonl (jsonl)

Thanks — will follow up once NDA is returned and sandbox is provisioned.

—
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0199


From: Ellie James <ellie.james@helixthera.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@helixthera.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Oct 2029 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery + proposed eval plan

Thanks Marcus — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

- Procurement & compliance: we need SOC 2 Type II and an insurance certificate before any dedicated sandbox (we’ll accept SOC 2 report for initial eval). Procurement contact is Priya Rao (procurement@helixthera.com) — she’ll expect a simple deliverable list.
- Schema behavior: we prefer strict schema validation for the production path (fail fast + structured error envelope). For the evaluation phase, we’d like a side-by-side mode where you return both the best-effort JSON and the validation result so we can measure repair strategies.
- Sandbox: yes please — we’d like a dedicated sandbox endpoint with predictable throughput and separate logs for the 14-day evaluation.

On models: we’re comfortable starting with Redwood-llama-13b-quant as the primary; if we see gaps we’ll opt to flip to Mistral-Instruct in narrower flows.

I’ve signed the NDA draft and uploaded it: Helix_NDA_redwood_v1.pdf (attached). Please send a DocuSign link and sandbox creds when ready.

—
Ellie James
Product & Integrations Lead | Helix Therapeutics
ellie.james@helixthera.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellie James <ellie.james@helixthera.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@helixthera.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Oct 2029 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery + proposed eval plan — provisioning & test plan

Following up on Marcus’ note and Ellie’s asks — I’ll own provisioning and the smoke-run. High level plan and action items from Redwood: 

1) NDA & procurement artifacts
- Marcus: send DocuSign link for Helix_NDA_redwood_v1.pdf (Ellie attached a signed copy; legal will counter-sign).
- Neha: package SOC 2 evidence + insurance cert into the secure drive link for Priya Rao.

2) Sandbox provisioning (48h) - Dedicated API endpoint with user-scoped API key
- Separate logs and a webhook for schema-failure events
- Rate-limited to Helix expected footprint (we’ll start at 1k req/day)

3) JSON schema compliance smoke-run (48-72h)
- Run the attached jsonschema_testcases.jsonl (1000 vectors) through the primary model (redwood-13b-quant) and report: schema_pass_rate, common failure paths, top 10 invalid fields by frequency.
- Output format: line-delimited JSON with fields: request_id, schema_valid (true/false), failure_paths, model_choice, latency_ms (we’ll share example output format in the sandbox).

4) 14-day eval & regression monitoring - Two model config experiment: primary=redwood-13b-quant; fallback=mistral-instruct.
- Metrics: schema_pass_rate, precision/recall on labeled extraction fields, p50/p95 latency, cost/token.
- Regression alerting: we’ll wire a daily eval job that compares rolling-window quality vs. your gold labels and fires an alert if avg F1 drops > 3%.

Retry/Idempotency recommendations
- Use idempotency-key header for client retries.
- Exponential backoff policy: 250ms -> 750ms -> 2000ms (max 3 tries) for 5xx/transient networking failures.
- For schema failures we recommend NOT automatically retrying unless the failure is tagged as "transient-parse"; we’ll include a failure_reason taxonomy in the webhook.

Open question for Helix
- Confirm whether you want us to return the failed-response + envelope to the same HTTP 200 body, or use 422 for schema-validation failures. We can support either; for analytics and visibility we prefer 200 + envelope.

Timeline
- NDA and DocuSign: today/tomorrow
- Sandbox: within 48 hours after NDA
- Smoke-run results: 48-72 hours after sandbox
- Eval start target: Oct 06 2029 (assuming sandbox creds by Oct 4)

I’ll attach a short runbook link in the sandbox with the example output format. Marcus — can you send the DocuSign link and the initial sandbox URL when available?

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Solutions Team | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
